title: Acute Pyelonephritis in Pregnancy: Assessment, Admission and Follow-Up

evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant patients with suspected acute pyelonephritis; recognition, cultures, hospital assessment and obstetric follow-up.
findings: Rebuilt against the approved-topic structure: a tiered investigation panel, time-ordered management and an explicit medicine decision pathway.
Every investigation row includes a reference or normal state, condition finding and next action.
Previous outline and published rows remain preserved; this additive version is pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was found in the opened Saudi Ministry of Health protocol index unless a Saudi source is explicitly cited in the medicine row.
Current live Saudi Food and Drug Authority product registration was not individually confirmed; clinicians must check the hospital formulary.
Local antibiogram, resistance pattern, shared-care agreement and imaging availability require site-level confirmation where relevant.

pathophysiology.summary: Ascending urinary infection can involve the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Pregnancy-related urinary stasis increases the risk of upper-tract infection. Systemic infection can cause sepsis, acute kidney injury and uterine activity.
keyMechanisms: Ascending urinary infection can involve the renal pelvis and parenchyma.
Pregnancy-related urinary stasis increases the risk of upper-tract infection.
Systemic infection can cause sepsis, acute kidney injury and uterine activity.

symptoms: Fever or rigors with flank or back pain.
Dysuria, frequency, urgency, nausea or vomiting may coexist.
physicalSigns: Fever, tachycardia, hypotension, dehydration or uterine activity.
redFlags: Sepsis physiology, hypotension, altered mental state, oliguria, persistent vomiting or concern about preterm labour.
precipitants: Recent urinary infection, urinary obstruction, renal stone, diabetes or urinary instrumentation.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Urinary symptoms without fever or flank tenderness.
Colicky pain and haematuria; fever raises concern for infected obstruction.
Focal abdominal signs without a urinary source; pregnancy can alter pain location.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Fever with flank pain or costovertebral-angle tenderness plus urinalysis/culture evidence supports acute pyelonephritis.
Refer if signs suggest sepsis or serious illness, dehydration or inability to take oral fluids/medicines; pregnancy lowers the threshold for specialist assessment (NG111 1.1.4–1.1.5).

ruleIn.normalValue: Temperature 36.0–37.5 °C; systolic blood pressure at least 90 mmHg; alert mental state
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Fever, tachycardia, hypotension, altered mentation or oliguria
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Treat physiological instability as sepsis; obtain senior obstetric and medical review without waiting for imaging.

ruleIn.normalValue: No nitrite, leucocyte esterase or blood
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Pyuria and/or nitrite; haematuria may occur
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Supports a urinary source but does not identify susceptibility.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: A urinary pathogen with a susceptibility profile
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Collect before antibiotics when this does not delay treatment; narrow treatment to the result.

ruleIn.normalValue: White-cell count 4.0–11.0 ×10⁹/L; haemoglobin and platelets within pregnancy-adjusted range
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Assesses inflammatory response and complications; use local pregnancy ranges.

ruleIn.normalValue: Creatinine within the pregnancy-adjusted laboratory range; potassium 3.5–5.0 mmol/L
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Acute kidney injury or electrolyte disturbance
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Guides fluid treatment and antimicrobial dose adjustment.

ruleIn.testName: Lactate and blood cultures when systemically unwell
ruleIn.normalValue: Lactate below 2 mmol/L; blood cultures no growth
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Identifies sepsis severity and bacteraemia; do not delay antibiotics in an unstable patient.

ruleOut.normalValue: No uterine activity; fetal assessment appropriate for gestation
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Contractions, fetal concern or threatened preterm labour
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Determines obstetric monitoring and location of care.
Use for suspected obstruction, recurrent disease or failure to improve.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess mother and fetus
actions: Use an ABCDE assessment, record sepsis physiology and obtain obstetric review.
Send urine culture before treatment when feasible; do not delay emergency treatment in sepsis.

clinicalManagement.title: Admit or obtain urgent specialist assessment
actions: Pregnancy with suspected upper urinary infection requires obstetric/medical assessment and a low threshold for admission.
Escalate suspected infected obstruction to urology.

clinicalManagement.title: Review response and results
actions: Review culture and narrow treatment through the local antimicrobial pathway.
Reassess persistent fever, pain or physiological abnormality for obstruction, abscess or an alternative diagnosis.

branches.label: Pregnant, stable and able to take oral medicine
branches.entryCriteria: Pregnant patient with acute pyelonephritis who is clinically stable, can take oral treatment and has a specialist-approved outpatient plan

branches.label: Pregnant, vomiting or severely unwell
branches.entryCriteria: Pregnant patient who is vomiting, unable to take oral medicine or severely unwell; admit and use the hospital intravenous pathway

medicationPlan.note: Review intravenous treatment by 48 hours and step down to oral treatment when possible. Check culture, allergy, renal function and the hospital antibiogram. Current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed; check the hospital formulary.

regimens.patientGroup: Pregnant patient, clinically stable and able to take oral medicine
regimens.dose: 500 mg; for severe infection the source permits 1–1.5 g per dose
regimens.frequency: Twice or three times daily; severe infection three or four times daily
adjustments: Use culture results to narrow treatment.
Adjust for renal impairment using the product label and local pharmacy guidance.
Check hospital formulary; current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed.
monitoring: Temperature, blood pressure, symptoms and oral intake within 24–48 hours.
contraindications: Use caution with a serious immediate penicillin allergy and seek microbiology advice.
regimens.branch: Pregnant, stable and able to take oral medicine

regimens.patientGroup: Pregnant patient who is vomiting, unable to take oral medicine or severely unwell
regimens.duration: Review at 48 hours; step down to oral treatment when possible to complete the specialist-defined course
adjustments: Dose at the higher end for severe infection.
Reduce in renal impairment using the product label and pharmacy guidance.
Check hospital formulary; cefuroxime is listed in the Saudi Essential Medicines List, but current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed.
monitoring: Maternal observations, renal function and response at least daily.
contraindications: Use caution with a serious immediate penicillin allergy and seek microbiology advice.

teaching.scope: Pregnant patients with suspected acute pyelonephritis; recognition, cultures, hospital assessment and obstetric follow-up.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Sepsis physiology, hypotension, altered mental state, oliguria, persistent vomiting or concern about preterm labour.
Review culture and narrow treatment through the local antimicrobial pathway.
pitfalls: Stopping after a short outline instead of documenting the full investigation pathway.
Using a medicine row without checking the branch, allergy, organ function, culture result and local formulary.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval; this version remains pending until a clinician approves it.

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: Afebrile and haemodynamically stable, tolerating oral intake, fetal/obstetric concerns addressed, culture follow-up and return plan documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Confirm culture response and arrange obstetric follow-up; repeat urine testing only as directed by the obstetric or microbiology plan.
